title.en: Summarise a study for the study group
title.es: Resumir un estudio para el grupo de estudio

es: Resumir un estudio sencillo ante el grupo con registro académico: objetivo, método, resultado, una pasiva impersonal y una respuesta prudente a una duda.

teaching.en: Briefly, the aim was to compare two groups of adults over eight weeks; it is worth noting that all were volunteers.
teaching.es: Brevemente, el objetivo era comparar dos grupos de adultos durante ocho semanas; conviene señalar que todos eran voluntarios.
teaching.explanationEs: Briefly abre un resumen condensado; it is worth noting introduce un dato que matiza lo anterior.
segments: Briefly, the aim was to compare two groups of adults over
eight weeks; it is worth noting that all were volunteers.
teaching.audioText: Briefly, the aim was to compare two groups of adults over eight weeks; it is worth noting that all were volunteers.

teaching.en: It is widely assumed that exercise sharpens memory, although that idea has rarely been tested in a controlled trial.
teaching.es: Se da por supuesto que el ejercicio agudiza la memoria, aunque esa idea rara vez se ha puesto a prueba en un ensayo controlado.
teaching.explanationEs: La pasiva impersonal presenta una opinión general sin decir quién la sostiene; it es obligatorio en inglés.
segments: It is widely assumed that exercise sharpens memory, although that
idea has rarely been tested in a controlled trial.
teaching.audioText: It is widely assumed that exercise sharpens memory, although that idea has rarely been tested in a controlled trial.

teaching.en: It has been shown that daily walkers scored higher, yet part of the difference can be attributed to motivation.
teaching.es: Se ha demostrado que quienes caminan a diario obtuvieron mejores puntuaciones, pero parte de la diferencia puede atribuirse a la motivación.
teaching.explanationEs: It has been shown = resultado establecido; be attributed to introduce una explicación posible.
segments: It has been shown that daily walkers scored higher, yet
part of the difference can be attributed to motivation.
teaching.audioText: It has been shown that daily walkers scored higher, yet part of the difference can be attributed to motivation.

teaching.en: The effect is thought to be small, and a pilot study of forty adults cannot account for every variable.
teaching.es: Se piensa que el efecto es pequeño, y un estudio piloto con cuarenta adultos no puede explicar todas las variables.
teaching.explanationEs: Variante personal de la impersonal: sujeto + be + participio + to + verbo; account for = explicar.
segments: The effect is thought to be small, and a pilot
study of forty adults cannot account for every variable.
teaching.audioText: The effect is thought to be small, and a pilot study of forty adults cannot account for every variable.

teaching.en: Overall, the benefit is small, and it is difficult to generalise from one group of volunteers to everyone.
teaching.es: En conjunto, el beneficio es pequeño, y es difícil generalizar a partir de un grupo de voluntarios a todo el mundo.
teaching.explanationEs: Overall condensa el resultado; it is difficult to generalise es la respuesta prudente ante quien pregunta si vale para todos.
segments: Overall, the benefit is small, and it is difficult
to generalise from one group of volunteers to everyone.
teaching.audioText: Overall, the benefit is small, and it is difficult to generalise from one group of volunteers to everyone.

teaching.en: On balance, the conclusion is tentative; it is thought to hold for adults, with the proviso that no teenagers were tested.
teaching.es: Sopesándolo todo, la conclusión es provisional; se piensa que vale para adultos, con la salvedad de que no se probó con adolescentes.
teaching.explanationEs: On balance cierra el resumen con un juicio global; with the proviso that añade la condición que limita la conclusión.
segments: On balance, the conclusion is tentative; it is thought to hold
for adults, with the proviso that no teenagers were tested.

prompt.es: Completa: «Se ha demostrado que dormir bien ayuda a la memoria.»

feedback.es: La pasiva impersonal es It has been + participio + that; shown presenta un resultado ya establecido.

hint.es: Participio de show: It has been ___ that…

origin.text: Researchers do not always name who holds an idea. They write instead: It has been ___ that regular sleep improves memory, although the effect is small.

prompt.es: ¿Qué frase es una pasiva impersonal bien formada y cautelosa?

choices.text: Is thought that the effect is small and may not apply to older adults.
It thinks that the effect is small and may not apply to older adults.
It is thought that the effect is small and may not apply to older adults.

feedback.es: La estructura correcta necesita it como sujeto y be + participio: It is thought that…; las otras dos omiten el sujeto o usan un verbo activo.

hint.es: En inglés el sujeto it es obligatorio; el verbo va en pasiva.

origin.text: You want to report a finding without saying who holds the view, and you want to sound cautious about how far it applies.

prompt.es: Ordena: «Brevemente, el objetivo era comparar dos grupos de adultos.»

answer.text: Briefly, the aim was to compare two groups of adults
accepted: Briefly, the aim was to compare two groups of adults
Briefly the aim was to compare two groups of adults

feedback.es: Briefly abre el resumen; the aim was to + verbo enuncia el objetivo en pasado.

hint.es: Briefly va al principio, seguido de una coma.

prompt.es: Escucha y elige qué concluye el hablante.

choices.text: The benefit is small, and nobody knows yet whether it applies elsewhere or grows with age.
The benefit is small, though it is certain to apply to other classes and age groups.
The benefit is small, and the study shows that it would be stronger with older students.

feedback.es: El hablante dice que el beneficio es pequeño y difícil de generalizar, y que un efecto mayor con estudiantes mayores es solo una suposición («nobody has tested that yet»).

origin.audio: Overall, the study suggests a small benefit, but the sample came from only one class, so it is difficult to generalise. It is thought that the effect would be stronger with older students, although nobody has tested that yet.

prompt.es: Un compañero pregunta si el resultado vale para todos. ¿Qué respuesta es la más prudente?

choices.text: It has been shown that the result holds for everyone, since they were volunteers.
It is difficult to generalise, since the participants were few, young and volunteers.
It is widely assumed that volunteers think like everybody else, so the answer is yes.

feedback.es: La respuesta prudente reconoce el límite de la muestra con it is difficult to generalise; las otras dos extienden el resultado sin pruebas.

origin.text: A classmate asks whether the walking results apply to everyone. The study involved forty adults, all of them volunteers, and all under thirty.

prompt.es: Completa: «En conjunto, los resultados son alentadores.»

feedback.es: Overall condensa el balance del estudio al comienzo de la frase.

origin.text: The study lasted only eight weeks and involved a single group. ___, the results are encouraging, but they should be treated as a first step.

prompt.es: ¿Qué postura transmite la autora de este resumen?

choices.text: Balanced: she weighs the result against its limits before she reaches a conclusion.
Critical of the study, which she thinks is too small to tell us anything.
Confident to the point of overstating what the study can actually show.
Neutral, simply repeating the authors' claims without any opinion of her own.

feedback.es: Dice «everyone should start walking today» a partir de una muestra de voluntarios y descarta ese límite como un detalle sin importancia: su seguridad va más allá de lo que el estudio permite.

origin.text: Briefly, the study compared two groups of adults over eight weeks. Overall, those who walked thirty minutes a day scored eight per cent higher on a memory test. It has been shown that exercise helps the mind, so everyone should start walking today. The study itself used only volunteers, but that detail did not seem worth a mention.

prompt.es: Escucha y elige cómo responde el ponente a la pregunta del público.

choices.text: Not yet: the result is promising but cannot safely be extended to everyone.
Yes, in general: the findings match earlier work, so the result can be extended.
No: the pilot study was too small to show anything at all about exercise.

feedback.es: El ponente dice «Not quite»: el resultado es prometedor y coincide con trabajos previos, pero con voluntarios es difícil generalizar y faltan los mayores; tampoco descarta el efecto.

origin.audio: Someone asked me whether exercise improves memory for everyone. Not quite. The study followed sixty adults, all of them volunteers, and the improvement was about eight per cent. It is thought that exercise helps, and the findings are in line with earlier work, but it is difficult to generalise from volunteers. On balance, the conclusion is tentative, with the proviso that older adults were not tested. I should add that this was a pilot study with a small sample, so it is thought that a larger trial would give a clearer picture, but nobody can say for certain until it is carried out.

prompt.es: Completa: «Parte de la mejora puede atribuirse a que todos eran voluntarios entusiastas.»

feedback.es: Be attributed to significa «atribuirse a»; due to y ascribed to son variantes cercanas.

origin.text: The improvement is thought to be small, and part of it may be ___ to the fact that all the participants were eager volunteers.

prompt.es: Resume el estudio: objetivo, método, resultado, pasiva impersonal y respuesta.

answer.text: The aim of this study was to examine whether taking notes by hand helps students remember more than typing. Briefly, one hundred and twenty students were followed for three weeks, and half of them wrote their notes by hand. Overall, the students who wrote by hand recalled six per cent more in a final test. It is widely assumed that handwriting is better for memory, and these findings are in line with that idea. It is worth noting that part of the difference may be attributed to motivation, since those students were all volunteers. To answer your question, we cannot say that handwriting is better for everyone, because all the participants came from one college, and it is difficult to generalise from a single group. On balance, the conclusion is tentative, and further research with students of different ages is needed before anyone gives firm advice to students.
accepted: The aim of this study was to examine whether taking notes by hand helps students remember more than typing. Briefly, one hundred and twenty students were followed for three weeks, and half of them wrote their notes by hand. Overall, the students who wrote by hand recalled six per cent more in a final test. It is widely assumed that handwriting is better for memory, and these findings are in line with that idea. It is worth noting that part of the difference may be attributed to motivation, since those students were all volunteers. To answer your question, we cannot say that handwriting is better for everyone, because all the participants came from one college, and it is difficult to generalise from a single group. On balance, the conclusion is tentative, and further research with students of different ages is needed before anyone gives firm advice to students.

This study asked whether taking notes by hand is better for memory than typing them. Briefly, a hundred and twenty students took part for three weeks, and half of them wrote by hand. Overall, the handwriters remembered six per cent more in the final test. It is often believed that writing by hand helps memory, and the results are in line with that view. However, everybody came from the same college, so we cannot say that handwriting is better for all students; it is difficult to generalise from one school. It is worth noting that some of the difference could be attributed to motivation. The conclusion is tentative, and further research is needed.

The aim was to examine whether students who write their notes by hand remember more than students who type. Briefly, one hundred and twenty students were tested over three weeks, and half of them used pens. Overall, the handwriters recalled six per cent more. It is thought that handwriting slows people down and helps them think, which is in line with these findings. To answer your question, it is difficult to generalise, since every participant belonged to one college, and we cannot say that the method works for everyone. On balance, the conclusion is tentative, with the proviso that more research is needed with different groups of students.

feedback.es: Un resumen completo recorre objetivo, método, resultado y límite, usa una pasiva impersonal y responde a la duda con prudencia.

origin.text: Estudio: ¿tomar apuntes a mano ayuda a recordar más que escribirlos en el teclado? 120 estudiantes durante tres semanas; la mitad escribió a mano. Los que escribieron a mano recordaron un 6 % más en una prueba final. Todos venían de un mismo colegio. Un compañero pregunta: «¿Podemos decir que escribir a mano es mejor para la memoria?» Escribe el resumen, usa una pasiva impersonal y responde con cautela.

prompt.es: ¿Con qué propósito escribe la autora «I would not generalise beyond first-year students»?

choices.text: To limit her answer to the kind of students that the study actually examined.
To say that first-year students are the only ones who should revise in this way.
To refuse to answer her classmate's question about the paper.
To warn that the paper is unreliable because it is old.

feedback.es: Delimita su respuesta a los estudiantes del estudio: es la prudencia de quien no extiende el resultado más allá de la muestra.

origin.text: Dear group, here is the summary you asked for. The aim was to compare two methods of revision. It has been shown that testing yourself beats reading your notes again, but the effect is thought to be smaller for difficult topics. I would not generalise from first-year students to students in later years. I hope that answers your question, and I am happy to share the paper.

prompt.es: Ordena: «Se cree ampliamente que el efecto es pequeño.»

answer.text: It is widely believed that the effect is small

feedback.es: It is widely believed that + oración es la pasiva impersonal con un adverbio de grado; it es obligatorio.

prompt.es: Relaciona cada fórmula del resumen con su sentido.

pairs: The difference can be attributed to…

feedback.es: Cada fórmula cumple una función: dar un resultado establecido, añadir un matiz, explicar una diferencia y cerrar con un balance.
